title: Rhoform Diagnostic v0
description: ONE line of the A1 newline-delimited JSON diagnostic stream (requirement A1: stable codes, byte spans, structured params separate from message strings, fix-its with applicability levels, deterministic capped output). The stream itself is zero or more of these objects, one per line, in the canonical order rhoform/diagnostics.py defines; each line stands alone, which is why files are named by repository-relative path here rather than through a stream-level file table. Emitted only by rhoform.diagnostics; the registry in rhoform/codes.py is the sole source of codes, slugs, severities and categories, and the registry gate holds the two in step. The spec's diagnostics section (spec/language/06-diagnostics.md) is the normative prose for this format.

^x_.description: Reserved extension point, scalars only (the same rule the part-data schema learned the hard way: structured x_ members hide defects from negative controls).

schema.description: Format discriminator. This schema describes version 0; a breaking change to any field ships as rhoform-diagnostic/1, never as a silent mutation.

code.description: The stable registry code. RHO + exactly four digits; the leading digit is the block (0 framework, 1 syntax, 2 elaboration, 3 types, 4 ground-architecture, 5 verification, 6 parts, 7 interop). A code means one thing forever; retired codes are never reassigned.

slug.description: The code's kebab-case slug, denormalized from the registry so a human reading one line needs no lookup table.

severity.description: error gates (V1), warning annotates, note carries non-gating context (safety notes, the truncation marker). Fixed per code in the registry; waivers (T6) downgrade at the reporting layer, not here.

category.description: The code's block name, denormalized from the registry.

tier.description: The V1 assertion tier, when the diagnostic reports an assertion result — V1 makes the tier visible in every diagnostic. Null for diagnostics that are not assertion results.

message.description: The human-rendered message. RENDERED from the registry template and the params — it can never say something the params do not — so consumers that want structure read params and consumers that want prose read this, and the two cannot disagree.

params.description: The structured parameters, exactly the set the registry declares for the code (enforced at emission; a JSON Schema cannot express the per-code contract, the registry gate does). Values are JSON scalars or arrays of scalars.

entity.description: The IR entity identity this diagnostic anchors to (instance/assertion path or net name), per the source-map schema's diagnostic-anchor rule; spans below are its resolution through the map. Null for pre-elaboration stages (lexer, parser), which have no IR to anchor to and carry raw spans.

spans.description: Byte spans into the author's own files, exactly one primary. Field vocabulary is ir/source-map.schema.json's: byte offsets authoritative, line/col denormalized.

fixits.description: Suggested fixes, possibly none. Ordered by preference; an agent applying a machine-applicable fix-it verbatim is expected to re-run the check, not to trust it blindly.

file.description: Repository-relative POSIX path of the source file. Never absolute, never host-specific (determinism contract).

byte_start.description: 0-based byte offset of the first byte of the span.

byte_end.description: 0-based byte offset one past the last byte (end-exclusive); >= byte_start. Equal offsets are an insertion point.

line_start.description: 1-based line of the span's first character.

col_start.description: 1-based column of the span's first character, counted in Unicode scalar values.

line_end.description: 1-based line of the span's last character.

col_end.description: 1-based column just past the span's last character.

primary.description: Exactly one span per diagnostic is primary; the canonical emission order sorts on it.

label.description: What this span shows the reader (e.g. "declared here", "instantiated from"). Null when the span speaks for itself.

replacement.description: Text replacing the span's bytes. A zero-length span makes this an insertion; an empty replacement makes it a deletion. Under has-placeholders, <name> markers appear here and are declared in the fix-it's placeholders.

applicability.description: machine-applicable: applying the edits verbatim is believed correct. needs-review: concrete edits, human judgment required. has-placeholders: the edits carry <name> markers the author must fill (this is how a fix-it INSERTS a component with a synthesized name, per the ground-architecture checker notes).

placeholders.description: Every <name> marker present in the edits, declared so a literal angle-bracket text can never be mistaken for a placeholder. Non-empty exactly when applicability is has-placeholders.

edits.description: At least one edit: a fix with no edit is a message, and messages belong in the diagnostic.
